original_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let k[x1, ..., xn] with n > 1, let Aut*_k(k[x1, ..., xn]) be the subgroup of polynomial automorphisms with Jacobian determinant 1, and let T = {diag(t1, ..., tn) | product_{i=1}^n ti = 1} be the diagonal torus acting by xi -> ti xi. What are the centralizer and the normalizer of T inside Aut*_k(k[x1, ..., xn])?
target_in_paper: Section 1 ("Roots of the Affine Cremona Group"), Problem 1.2: "Describe the centralizer and the normalizer of T in G." This is the exact official problem your draft is targeting. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/math/0504517))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s target almost exactly. It has the correct ambient field assumptions (k algebraically closed, char 0), the correct polynomial algebra in n > 1 variables, the correct subgroup Aut*_k of Jacobian-1 polynomial automorphisms, the correct diagonal torus T with product t1⋯tn = 1 acting by xi ↦ ti xi, and it asks for exactly the two objects named in the paper: the centralizer and the normalizer of T inside that group. In substance, this is Problem 1.2 with the paper’s shorthand notation expanded. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/math/0504517))
missing_details: The paper introduces the shorthand k^[n] := k[x1,...,xn] and G := Aut*_k(k^[n]) immediately before Problem 1.2; the official formulation is in terms of T inside G. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/math/0504517))

It is worth making explicit that each ti lies in k^×, so T is the standard diagonal (n−1)-dimensional torus of volume-preserving linear automorphisms. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/math/0504517))

The centralizer and normalizer should be explicitly understood as C_G(T) and N_G(T), i.e. taken inside G = Aut*_k(k^[n]), not inside the full affine Cremona group Aut_k(k^[n]). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/math/0504517))

No extra hypotheses from the neighboring root-vector discussion should be added: Problem 1.2 does not involve locally nilpotent derivations, characters, homogeneity, degree restrictions, or any asymptotic clause such as 'for all sufficiently large m'. Those belong to Definition 1.1 / Problem 1.1, not to Problem 1.2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/math/0504517))
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, let k^[n] = k[x1,...,xn] with n > 1, and let G = Aut*_k(k^[n]) = {σ ∈ Aut_k(k^[n]) : Jac(σ) = 1}. Let T = {diag(t1,...,tn) ∈ G : ti ∈ k^× and t1⋯tn = 1}, acting by xi ↦ ti xi. Describe the centralizer C_G(T) and the normalizer N_G(T).
justification: The draft is aiming at Section 1, Problem 1.2, not at the neighboring root-vector problem. In the paper, the notation k^[n], G = Aut*_k(k^[n]), and the diagonal torus T are set up immediately before the official statement, which then asks only for the centralizer and normalizer of T in G. So the sharpest faithful rewrite is simply the official Problem 1.2 with those abbreviations expanded into a stand-alone question. The remark after Problem 1.2 discusses a different issue—linearizability of volume-preserving torus actions and maximal (n−1)-dimensional tori—so it should not be promoted to an alternate formulation of this problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/math/0504517))
